people.name: Dougie Poynter
people.description: Dougie Poynter provides bass and vocals for the British pop rock band McFly. The group achieved a UK No.1 single in 2004 with 'Colours In Her Hair' and a UK No.1 album the same year with Room On The 3rd Floor. This achievement earned them a Guinness Book of Records entry as the youngest band ever to have an album debut at No.1, a distinction previously held by The Beatles. The band derived its name from Marty McFly, a character in the film Back to the Future.

people.name: Clay Aiken
people.description: Clay Aiken is an American singer, television personality, actor, and political activist. He placed as the runner-up on the US American Idol in 2003 and achieved a US No. 1 single that same year with "This Is The Night". His debut album, Measure of a Man (2003), entered the US Billboard 200 chart at No. 1, marking the highest-selling debut for a solo artist since Snoop Dogg's Doggystyle in December 1993.

people.name: Mindy McCready
people.description: American country music singer Mindy McCready placed twelve singles on the Billboard country singles charts across her first four studio albums. At the age of 37, she died on February 17, 2013 from a self-inflicted gunshot wound on her front porch. This was the same location where David Wilson, who was her former boyfriend and the father of her younger son, had died from a fatal self-inflicted gunshot one month earlier. Prior to her suicide, she also shot and killed Wilson's pet dog.

people.name: John Moyer
people.description: John Moyer is the bassist for the American heavy metal band Disturbed, which achieved a US No.1 album in 2005 with Ten Thousand Fists. The group has sold more than 17 million records globally, earned two Grammy Award nominations, and placed singles from all eight of their albums into the top ten of the Mainstream Rock chart.

people.name: Des\'ree
people.description: Des'ree is an English pop and soul recording artist and songwriter who gained fame in the 1990s. Recognized for her unique contralto voice and positive lyrics, her major hits comprise the singles 'Feel So High', 'You Gotta Be', and 'Life', alongside the ballad 'Kissing You', which appeared on the soundtrack for the 1996 film Romeo + Juliet. She received the award for Best British Female at the 1999 Brit Awards.

people.name: Paul Wheeler
people.description: Paul Wheeler is a member of the Australian rock band Icehouse, which achieved a UK hit single in 1983 with 'Hey Little Girl'. The group's most recognized singles on the Australian charts include 'Great Southern Land', 'Crazy', and 'Electric Blue'.

people.name: Cherie Currie
people.description: Cherie Currie is an American singer, musician, actress, and artist who served as the lead vocalist for the Los Angeles rock band the Runaways during the mid-to-late 1970s. The group's well-known songs include 'Cherry Bomb', 'Hollywood', and 'Queens of Noise'. In 1980, Currie teamed up with her identical twin sister, Marie Currie, to release the album Messin' With The Boys under the duo name Cherie & Marie Currie.

people.name: Stacey Q
people.description: Stacey Swain is an American pop singer, songwriter, dancer and actress who performs under the stage name Stacey Q. Released in 1986, her best-known single 'Two of Hearts' climbed to No. 1 in Canada, hit No. 3 on the US Billboard Hot 100, and entered the top ten in five other countries.

people.name: Richard Barbieri
people.description: Richard Barbieri served as the keyboardist [[LINK_N]] for the English new wave band Japan, which scored a UK No.5 single in 1982 with 'Ghosts'. Starting out as a glam rock-inspired group, Japan evolved their musical style and androgynous aesthetic to embrace art rock, electronic music, and foreign influences.

people.name: John Ashton
people.description: John Ashton is a guitarist for the English rock band The Psychedelic Furs. The film director John Hughes featured their song 'Pretty in Pink' in his 1986 film sharing the same name.

people.name: Billy Idol
people.description: William Broad, known as Billy Idol, is an English singer, songwriter, musician, and actor. While performing with Generation X, he achieved a 1979 UK No.11 single with 'King Rocker', and the group became one of the first punk bands to appear on the BBC Television music programme Top of the Pops. Idol later pursued a solo career, gaining international recognition and emerging as a lead artist during America's MTV-driven "Second British Invasion" through the music videos for his singles 'Dancing with Myself' and 'White Wedding'. He achieved the 1987 US No.1 and UK No.7 single 'Mony Mony', alongside nine additional UK top 40 singles.

people.name: George McArdale
people.description: George McArdale was a member of the Australian band Little River Band. The group achieved a 1978 US No. 3 single with 'Reminiscing' and landed 12 additional US Top 40 singles, ultimately selling more than 30 million records.

people.name: Johnny Shuggie Otis
people.description: American singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Johnny Shuggie Otis wrote the composition 'Strawberry Letter 23'. Recorded by The Brothers Johnson, the track topped the Billboard R&B chart and reached No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in 1977.

people.name: David Sancious
people.description: David Sancious plays keyboards and guitar and was an early member of Bruce Springsteen's E Street Band. He performed on the first three Springsteen albums and has collaborated with Stanley Clarke, Narada Michael Walden, Zucchero Fornaciari, Eric Clapton, Peter Gabriel, and Sting, along with numerous other artists.

people.name: June Pointer
people.description: June Pointer was a vocalist for the American R&B vocal group The Pointer Sisters, known for their 1981 US No. 2 single "Slow Hand" and their 1984 UK No. 2 single "Automatic." The Pointer Sisters earned three Grammy Awards and secured 13 US top 20 hits spanning from 1973 to 1985. She passed away in Santa Monica, California, on 11 April 2006 at the age of 52.

people.name: Roger Glover
people.description: Roger Glover is a Welsh bassist, songwriter, and record producer best known for his work with Deep Purple, contributing to releases such as the 1970 UK No.2 single 'Black Night' and the 1973 US No.4 single 'Smoke On The Water'. The band was recognized in the 1975 Guinness Book of World Records as "the globe's loudest band" following a 1972 performance at London's Rainbow Theatre, and they have achieved worldwide sales exceeding 100 million records.

people.name: Rob Grill
people.description: Rob Grill, alongside the band Grass Roots, achieved a 1968 US No.5 single with 'Midnight Confessions', in addition to 13 other US Top 40 singles. At the age of 67, Grill passed away on 11th July 2011 following a head injury sustained from a fall brought on by a stroke.

people.name: J. J. Barnesm
people.description: American R&B singer and songwriter J. J. Barnesm released early tracks such as 'Just One More Time' and 'Please Let Me In', which subsequently became popular Northern soul favourites in the UK. He passed away on December 10, 2022, at the age of 79.

people.name: Leo Lyons
people.description: English musician, Leo Lyons who was the bassist in,Ten Years After. They scored the 1970 No.10 UK single 'Love Like A Man' and had eight consecutive albums in the Top 40 on the UK Albums Chart between 1968 and 1973. The band performed a breakthrough American appearance at the Woodstock Festival, their rendition of 'I'm Going Home' with Alvin Lee as lead singer/lead guitarist was featured in both the subsequent film and soundtrack album, and increased the group's popularity.

people.name: Frank Ifield
people.description: Frank Ifield was a British-born Australian country music singer and guitarist who frequently included yodelling in his songs. During the early 1960s, he achieved four No. 1 hits on the UK Singles Chart with his cover versions of 'I Remember You', 'Lovesick Blues', 'The Wayward Wind', and 'Confessin' That I Love You'. Ifield passed away from pneumonia on 18 May 2024 at the age of 86.

people.name: Bob Moore
people.description: Bob Moore was an American double bassist, orchestra leader, and session musician. During the 1950s and 1960s, he belonged to the Nashville A-Team and played on more than 17,000 documented recording sessions, providing backing for artists including Elvis Presley, Patsy Cline, Bob Dylan, and Roy Orbison. He passed away on 22 September 2021.

people.name: Dick Clark
people.description: Dick Clark served as the host of the longest-running music show on United States television, American Bandstand, and created and produced the annual American Music Awards. Clark passed away on April 18, 2012.

people.name: Allan Sherman
people.description: Allan Sherman was an American musician, comedian, and television producer who gained recognition as a song parodist during the early 1960s. In 1963, he released the single 'Hello Muddah, Hello Faddah', which reached No.2 in the US and No.14 in the UK. This song earned a Grammy Award for Best Comedy Performance at the 6th Annual Grammy Awards in 1964. Sherman passed away on 20 November 1973 at his home in Los Angeles while entertaining friends, just ten days before turning 49.

people.name: Brownie McGhee
people.description: Brownie McGhee was an American folk music and blues singer and guitarist. He is best known for his collaboration with the harmonica player Sonny Terry. McGhee died of stomach cancer on 16 February 1996 in Oakland, California, aged 80.

works.title: Fairytale of New York
works.eventDescription: Shane MacGowan, frontman of the Irish punk band Pogue Mahone—later shortened to The Pogues—which he formed in 1982 and with whom he released seven studio albums, has died at the age of 65. The singer-songwriter, whose well-documented struggles included issues with drugs and alcohol, had been in poor health for some time and recently spent time in the hospital following an encephalitis diagnosis. His notable hits feature 1987's 'Fairytale of New York' and 'A Pair of Brown Eyes'.

works.title: Don’t Stop
works.eventDescription: English singer and musician Christine McVie passed away from a stroke at 79 years old. Within Fleetwood Mac, she served as a vocalist, songwriter, and keyboardist. During the mid-1960s British Blues scene, McVie performed in various groups, most notably Chicken Shack. Her collaboration with Fleetwood Mac began in 1968 as a session player, and she officially became a band member two years afterward. A 1988 Greatest Hits album by Fleetwood Mac featured eight tracks she either wrote or co-wrote, such as 'Little Lies', 'Everywhere', and 'Don't Stop'.

works.title: Can’t Get You Out of My Head
works.eventDescription: Manchester hosted the inaugural Top Of The Pops UK Awards, featuring viewer-voted categories from the BBC program. The winners comprised Westlife for Best pop act, Destiny's Child for Best R&B Act, U2 for Best Rock Act, Fatboy Slim for Best Dance Act, Nelly Furtado for Best Newcomer, Kylie Minogue's 'Can't Get You Out Of My Head' for Best Single, Travis's 'The Invisible Band' for Best Album, Jennifer Lopez as Artist on top of the world, and Paul McCartney for the Hall of Fame Award.

works.title: Working for the Weekend
works.eventDescription: Scott Smith bassist for the Canadian rock band Loverboy died age 45. He was sailing his boat with two friends off the coast of San Francisco near the Golden Gate Bridge, when a large wave swept him overboard. Loverboy were best known for their hit singles ‘Working for the Weekend’ and ‘Turn Me Loose’, although their US Top Ten hits were ‘Lovin' Every Minute of It’ in 1985 and ‘This Could Be the Night’. Loverboy sold over 23 million records and in 1986 the band won six Juno Awards in 1982. He also later worked as a late-night radio DJ at CFOX.

works.eventDescription: Elton John faced criticism from the Boy Scout Association following a performance at London's Albert Hall, where he sang 'It's A Sin' alongside six male dancers in Boy Scout uniforms who stripped off their outfits on stage.

works.title: Tiptoe Through the Tulips
works.eventDescription: American vocalist and ukulele performer Tiny Tim, whose birth name was Herbert Khaury, passed away following a heart attack while performing his popular song 'Tiptoe Through the Tulips' on stage at a Minneapolis venue. Victoria Mae Budinger and he wed on 17 December 1969 on The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson as a publicity event, drawing an audience of over 40 million television viewers, and subsequently had a daughter named Tulip Victoria. A crowd numbering 600,000 individuals attended his performance at the 1970 Isle Of Wight Festival.

works.title: Dangerous
works.eventDescription: Michael Jackson achieved his fourth UK No.1 album with his eighth studio release, Dangerous. Worldwide sales for the album have exceeded 32 million copies, positioning it among the best-selling albums in history.

works.title: "Another Brick in the Wall Part 2"
works.eventDescription: In 1979, Pink Floyd put out "Another Brick in the Wall Part 2", marking the group's first UK single since 1968's 'Point Me at the Sky' and securing their sole chart-topping single in the UK as the Christmas No.1 of that year. South Africa banned both the single and the album The Wall in 1980 after student protesters demonstrating against educational inequalities under apartheid during a nationwide school boycott adopted the track.

works.title: Wichita Lineman
works.eventDescription: Glen Campbell began a five-week tenure at No. 1 on the US album chart with 'Wichita Lineman.' The lyrics were inspired by Jimmy Webb while he was driving through Washita County in northern Oklahoma, passing an endless series of identical telephone poles. Spotting the silhouette of a lone lineman on a pole in the distance, Webb imagined himself on the pole holding the phone and pondered what the lineman might be saying into the receiver.

works.title: With The Beatles
works.eventDescription: The Beatles released their second album, With The Beatles, which marked the first time a group achieved million-selling status for an album in the UK. Holding the number-one chart position for 21 weeks and replacing Please Please Me, the achievement meant The Beatles maintained the top spot for a continuous 51 weeks.

works.title: I Remember You
works.eventDescription: Frank Ifield was a British-born Australian country music singer and guitarist who frequently included yodelling in his songs. During the early 1960s, he achieved four No. 1 hits on the UK Singles Chart with his cover versions of 'I Remember You', 'Lovesick Blues', 'The Wayward Wind', and 'Confessin' That I Love You'. Ifield passed away from pneumonia on 18 May 2024 at the age of 86.

works.title: Hello Muddah, Hello Faddah!
works.eventDescription: Allan Sherman was an American musician, comedian, and television producer who gained recognition as a song parodist during the early 1960s. In 1963, he released the single 'Hello Muddah, Hello Faddah', which reached No.2 in the US and No.14 in the UK. This song earned a Grammy Award for Best Comedy Performance at the 6th Annual Grammy Awards in 1964. Sherman passed away on 20 November 1973 at his home in Los Angeles while entertaining friends, just ten days before turning 49.
